title: Describing people
specPoints: My personal world: identity and relationships

tips.title: Hair and eyes take avoir, and are plural
tips.body: *Elle **a** les cheveux longs et les yeux bleus.* French *has* hair and eyes, with **les**, and the adjectives are **masculine plural** because *cheveux* and *yeux* are — *longs, bruns, frisés, bleus, verts*. Even for a girl.

tips.title: Marron never changes
tips.body: *Les yeux **marron**, les cheveux **marron**.* *Marron* is a noun (a chestnut) used as a colour, so it takes no *-s* and no *-e*. *Orange* is the same. Every other colour agrees: *bleus, verts, gris, noirs*.

tips.title: Size and build take être
tips.body: *Il **est** grand, petit, de taille moyenne, mince, gros.* Physical build is *être* + adjective, agreeing: *elle est grande et mince*. *Il mesure un mètre soixante-quinze* gives the exact height.

tips.title: Il porte, il a
tips.body: *Il **porte** des lunettes* (wears glasses), *il **a** une barbe / une moustache*, *elle **a** un tatouage*. *Porter* for things worn, *avoir* for things that are part of you.

tips.title: Avoir l'air for how someone seems
tips.body: *Elle **a l'air** sympa. Il **a l'air** fatigué.* (She seems nice, he looks tired.) *Avoir l'air* + adjective is the bridge from appearance to character, and it is the phrase that makes a description sound like a person rather than a list.

steps.title: Les cheveux et les yeux
steps.body:
A physical description starts with hair and eyes, and both use **avoir + les**.

**Hair** — *il / elle a les cheveux* + length + colour:

- length: *longs, courts, mi-longs* (shoulder-length)
- style: *raides* (straight), *frisés* (curly), *bouclés* (wavy)
- colour: *bruns, blonds, noirs, roux* (red / ginger), *châtains* (light brown), *gris, blancs*

*Elle a les cheveux longs et bruns.* The adjectives are masculine plural to agree with *cheveux* — never *longues*.

**Eyes** — *il / elle a les yeux* + *bleus, verts, gris, noirs, **marron***. *Marron* is **invariable**: *les yeux marron*, no *-s*.

*Il est chauve* (bald). *Il / elle est roux / rousse* — *roux* works as an adjective for the person too.

**Face and extras**: *il porte des lunettes* (glasses), *il a une barbe, une moustache*, *elle a des taches de rousseur* (freckles), *il a un tatouage*, *elle a un piercing*.

steps.title: La taille et l'apparence
steps.body:
**Build and height** use **être** + adjective, agreeing with the person.

*Il est **grand**, elle est **grande*** (tall); *petit(e)* (short); *de taille moyenne* (medium height); *mince* (slim); *gros / grosse* (fat — *un peu fort(e)* is the polite version); *musclé(e)*; *costaud* (well-built).

**Exact height**: *il mesure un mètre soixante-quinze* — 1 m 75, or 175 cm. *Elle mesure un mètre soixante.*

**Age and look**: *il a l'air jeune / vieux*, *elle fait plus jeune que son âge* (looks younger than her age), *il a environ quarante ans*.

**Overall**: *il est beau / elle est belle* (good-looking), *joli(e)* (pretty), *mignon / mignonne* (cute), *moche* (ugly — informal), *élégant(e)*, *il a un beau sourire* (a nice smile).

**Clothes and style**: *il porte toujours un jean et des baskets*, *elle est toujours bien habillée* (well dressed), *il a un style décontracté* (casual).

**Avoir l'air**: *elle a l'air sympa / sérieuse / fatiguée / triste* — the adjective agrees with the person.

steps.title: Comparer, et le passé
steps.body:
**Comparing people**: *ma sœur est **plus** grande **que** moi*, *mon frère est **moins** sportif **que** ma sœur*, *ils ont **les mêmes** yeux*, *on **se ressemble*** (we look alike), *il **ressemble à** son père* (he looks like his father).

**Superlatives**: *c'est le plus grand de la famille* (the tallest in the family), *elle est la plus jeune*.

**Then and now**: *avant, il avait les cheveux longs* (before, he had long hair — the imperfect *avait*), *maintenant il a les cheveux courts*. *Avait* and *était* are the two imperfect forms worth knowing before the imperfect is taught: *elle était petite, maintenant elle est grande*.

**Describing someone you saw** — for a reading text or a story: *j'ai vu un homme grand, aux cheveux gris, qui portait un manteau noir* (who was wearing a black coat). *Aux cheveux gris* — *with grey hair* — is a compact way to attach a feature to a noun.

**Asking**: *Il est comment ?* (What is he like?), *Elle ressemble à qui ?* (Who does she look like?), *De quelle couleur sont ses yeux ?*

steps.title: Your turn
steps.body:
**Part A.**

1. Describe your own hair and eyes with *j'ai les cheveux … et les yeux …*
2. Write *she is short and slim* and *he is tall and well-built*.
3. Write *brown eyes* and *blue eyes* — which one has no *-s*?

**Part B.**

4. Describe a family member: age, height, hair, eyes, glasses or beard.
5. Write how someone seems with *avoir l'air*.
6. Compare two people with *plus … que*.

**Part C.**

7. Write *before he had long hair, now he has short hair*.
8. Describe someone you saw with *aux cheveux …* and *qui portait …*
9. Write six sentences describing a friend or relative: appearance, style, how they seem, a comparison, and their character.

For question 9, hair and eye adjectives are masculine plural, and everything else agrees with the person.

steps.title: Going deeper
steps.body:
**Cheveux and yeux are masculine plural.** *Elle a les cheveux longs et les yeux verts* — never *longues*, never *vertes*, whoever the person is.

**Marron does not agree.** *Les yeux marron.* One of the two invariable colours (*orange* is the other).

**Être for build, avoir for features, porter for things worn.** Three verbs, and choosing the right one is most of the accuracy in this topic.

**Give the exact height.** *Il mesure un mètre soixante-quinze.* Numbers are detail, and *mesurer* is a verb the examiner rarely sees.

**Use avoir l'air to bridge to character.** *Elle a l'air timide, mais en fait elle est très bavarde.* Appearance, contrast, personality — three ideas in one sentence.

**Compare.** *Il est plus grand que moi mais moins sportif que ma sœur.* Two comparisons, one line.

**Then and now with avait / était.** *Avant, elle avait les cheveux longs; maintenant elle a les cheveux courts.* Two imperfect forms give you a past description without the whole tense.

**Attach features with aux.** *Un homme aux cheveux gris, une fille aux yeux bleus.* Compact, native, and a reading-text pattern worth recognising.

steps.title: Summary
steps.body:
- **Hair**: *il / elle a les cheveux* + *longs, courts, mi-longs, raides, frisés, bruns, blonds, noirs, roux, châtains, gris*.
- **Eyes**: *il / elle a les yeux* + *bleus, verts, gris, noirs, **marron***.
- *Cheveux* and *yeux* are **masculine plural**; *marron* is **invariable**.
- **Build**: *être* + *grand(e), petit(e), de taille moyenne, mince, gros / grosse, musclé(e)*.
- *Il mesure un mètre soixante-quinze.*
- **Extras**: *il porte des lunettes; il a une barbe, une moustache, des taches de rousseur*.
- **Looks**: *beau / belle, joli(e), mignon / mignonne, roux / rousse*.
- ***Avoir l'air*** + adjective: *elle a l'air sympa*.
- **Compare**: *plus / moins … que*, *le / la plus …*, *ressembler à*, *on se ressemble*.
- **Then and now**: *avant il avait …, maintenant il a …*; *elle était …*
- *Aux cheveux gris, aux yeux bleus.*
- *Il est comment ? De quelle couleur sont ses yeux ?*

examTechnique.body:
Hair and eyes take **avoir + les** with **masculine plural** adjectives and **marron** invariable; build takes **être** and agrees with the person; **porter** for things worn. Give the height with *mesurer* and the impression with **avoir l'air**.

Add a comparison with *plus / moins … que*, a superlative, and a then-and-now with *avait / était* for range.
examinerErrors: Il a des lunettes for wearing them.
Adjectives agreeing with the writer instead of the person described.
Present tense for a past appearance.
A list of features with no avoir l'air or character.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 description chooses *avoir*, *être* and *porter* correctly, makes every hair and eye adjective masculine plural and leaves *marron* alone, and agrees build and looks with the person. It gives an exact height, bridges to character with *avoir l'air* and a contrast, compares with *plus … que* and a superlative, and adds a then-and-now with *avait / était* or an *aux cheveux …* phrase.
